page: Amazon Web Services m8i.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture running at 3.9 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores via multithreading, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction sets are available, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

System memory comprises 32 GB of DDR5 operating at a 7 GHz transfer rate, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Local storage is not bundled with the instance, requiring external EBS volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. The platform contains no hardware graphics acceleration or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2104.0, strong gzip compression at 33.95 GB/sec, and top-tier text processing metrics at 2919.0. Multi-core execution lands in the median range with a stress-ng score of 8640.95 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8228.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 69.77 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput measures 15.51 GB/sec.

Given its balanced compute-to-memory allocation and modern instruction set support, m8i.2xlarge offers solid resource density for varied enterprise deployments. The server is well suited for backend microservices, web application hosting, CI/CD build environments, and in-memory key-value caching such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, alongside 480 MB of L3 cache and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Memory is provisioned at 32 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Baseline networking provides 4 Gbps throughput. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators, necessitating network storage attachments for persistent state. Synthetic testing reveals strong single-core computation, top-tier text processing, and solid single-thread compression speeds, while multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth show average throughput. This instance configuration is suited for backend microservices, web application clusters, software compilation pipelines, and mid-sized in-memory databases.
